correctness.rationale: Smoothness follows from the z derivative and squarefree binary quartic. Analytic local intersections are four A7 contacts and one ordinary fourfold point, giving tau=37. The explicit homogeneous syzygies (H_y,-H_x,0) and (xz^3,yz^3,2H-z^4) have degrees 3 and 4 and cross product exactly -grad f; the Saito criterion proves freeness. For any PGL3 equivalence, the unique nonlinear component and unique concurrent center imply a block-triangular map; comparing the z^3 and z^4 coefficients forces the lower shear to vanish and relates binary quartics by scalar, so all equivalences and automorphisms are exactly those of the unordered four-point root divisor with four central lifts. Standard anharmonic orbit sizes yield 16,32,48. Sympy verifier replayed these symbolic identities and representative group sizes. The universal classification depends on the algebraic proof, not finite samples.

originality.rationale: Source Theorem 1.5 proves the whole construction is free, but it neither identifies the projective equivalence classes of the reducible eight-degree curves nor determines their full stabilizers. The proof exploits intrinsic uniqueness of the quartic and of the four-line center, forces the z-shear to vanish by coefficient comparison, and determines a central fourfold lift of the four-point stabilizer. Smooth quartic G48/G96 classification does not determine the stabilizer of the marked line union; at the harmonic value they differ by index three. Relevant indexed mathematical records contain adjacent but distinct symmetry and conic-line results. Residual risk: an unindexed classical calculation may express the same conclusion.
residual_risks: Classical literature on cyclic quartics and four hyperflexes may state equivalent marked-family symmetries under an unfamiliar terminology.
Automorphism tables for smooth quartics are not exhaustive evidence for uniqueness of a theorem about reducible marked curves; the separate proof is decisive for mathematical content.

value.rationale: This is a complete projective classification of a natural positive-dimensional family of free plane curves: a smooth quartic together with its four maximal-order flex tangents, not merely another isolated free example or a numerical parameter substitution. It provides the precise one-dimensional moduli invariant, identifies every automorphism and both exceptional enhanced-symmetry loci, and exhibits an index-three symmetry drop when the harmonic component is the Fermat quartic. The gap is geometric: freeness is known for arbitrary factors, but the full geometric realization orbit and marking-preserving stabilizers were not addressed by that theorem. No speculative external application is required.
